input.quote: (a) In the event the Company terminates this Agreement, the Company shall pay to HDI a termination payment, (the "Termination Payment") the amount of which shall be an amount equal to the aggregate Net Sales for the twelve (12) months preceding the Termination Date less $800,000, the balance of which shall be divided by two.
input.rationale: Section 4.2 is the only liquidated amount in the Agreement and it runs against us: on any termination by the Company (subject only to the narrow "without penalty" carve-out in Section 1.6 for late launch) we must pay HDI 50% of the trailing twelve months' Net Sales above $800,000, in eight quarterly installments (p0026-p0029). Our fees under Section 3.1 are 30% of monthly Net Sales over $11,000, so three months' fees are roughly 7.5% of annual Net Sales, whereas the Termination Payment is 50% of annual Net Sales over $800,000 — many multiples of the fallback cap and capable of exceeding the remaining contract value, i.e. walk-away territory. It is also uncapped and triggered by any Company termination, including termination for HDI's own failure. Nothing else in the document imposes penalties or minimum fees on us (Section 1.6 benefits us and is not flagged). The redline takes the preferred position by removing the formula and stating that no termination payment, liquidated damages or penalty of any kind is payable by the Company; 4.2(b) and (c) remain only as conditional mechanics with no amount to which they can apply. As a fallback we could accept an early-termination fee capped at three months' fees as the sole liquidated amount.

mappings.element: Customer pays no liquidated damages or penalties.

proposal.summary: Remove the Company-payable Termination Payment formula in Section 4.2(a) and state that no liquidated amount is payable by the Company.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] Section 4.2 requires us to pay HDI 50% of the prior twelve months' Net Sales above $800,000 whenever we terminate, which can exceed both three months' fees and the remaining contract value. Our position is that no liquidated damages or penalties are payable by the Company, so we have deleted the termination payment; if a fee is unavoidable we could accept an early-termination fee capped at three months' fees as the sole liquidated amount.
